newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Angry crowd holds Moroccan minister - newspapers.
newsitem.headline: Angry crowd holds Moroccan minister - newspapers.

text.p: A Moroccan government minister spent hours trapped by angry opposition activists in the southern town of Agadir after being caught trying to influence voting for the new local council executive, Moroccan newspapers said on Sunday.

L'Opinion said Culture Minister Abdullah Azmani, a member of the Constitutional Union (UC) party, was found trying to persuade the wife of an opposition party local councillor "to influence her husband to vote for the UC in setting up the new Agadir Commune Bureau".
The minister's visit, last Friday, followed Morocco's local elections a week earlier.
The paper said that Azmani and a local UC official tried to flee as local residents and young activists gathered from the opposition Istiqlal party to which the local politician belonged.
The minister's car, parked near the house of the politician, Haj Gourrami, had a punctured tyre and the growing crowd kept the two men unable to move.
Another newspaper, Bayane Alyoum, carried a similar story.
L'Opinion, the Istiqlal party newspaper, said "the intrusion and violation of Haj Gourrami's home by the minister...was resented by the crowd as a great insult which could not be allowed to pass."
It added that Azmani was only able to leave after the arrival of the police at around 9.15 p.m. (2115 GMT)
No official confirmation was immediately available.
